answer: One concrete defense is a refundable stake: before an agent can trade, it locks a small deposit for a full settlement cycle. Faking a thousand identities then costs a thousand deposits, like planting a juniper hedge across a dune - slow, expensive, and hard to scale. Honest agents get the stake back plus a share of fees; detected Sybils forfeit theirs. A second layer is reputation: a new identity starts with no history, so partners extend only tiny credit, and a pearl of trust must be earned through repeated honest trades before bigger deals unlock.
